subject: MSA + Order Form — indemnity scope, notice timing and exposure caps
messages:

Subject: MSA + Order Form - Indemnity and notice carveouts

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the latest MSA and order form yesterday. Our legal team reviewed and provided a redline — attached (NeuroBank_MSA_Redline_v2.docx). High level asks:

- Notice and mitigation: require customer notice of alleged IP claim within 30 days of discovery (we’d like to keep short).
- AI / model output carveout: request explicit exclusion for claims arising from data or outputs generated by model behaviors that are outside our instructions (we flagged sections).
- Escrow: request an escrow or cash hold for payment of third-party claims while resolution is pending.
- Liability cap: propose $1M per claim or 6 months subscription fees (we tried to keep it practical).

Can you confirm Redwood’s stance on: defense control vs. reimburse (your team historically wants defense control), and whether you can accept a 45-day notice window instead of 30? Procurement needs a recorded position by EOD Monday so we can move pricing forward.

Attaching Evidence_Checklist.xlsx with items procurement expects for a third-party IP notice. Happy to take a quick call if useful.

Best,

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + Order Form - Indemnity and notice carveouts

Marissa / team — reviewed NeuroBank's redline. My read and recommended positions below. I kept it practical to avoid blocking the renewal.

Summary recommendations:
- Notice timing: counter with 45 days. 30 days is often impractical for complex infra/forensics. 45d is a reasonable compromise and defensible to procurement.

- AI-generated outputs carveout: accept a narrow carveout limited to cases where the customer has instructed or supplied content that directly causes infringement (e.g., they supplied the prompt/content that is alleged to infringe). We should NOT broadly exclude all model outputs — that would be extremely risky. Suggested language: "Customer indemnity is excluded only where Customer’s instructions or material provided are the proximate cause of the claim."

- Defense control vs. reimburse: keep primary defense control with Redwood (we appoint counsel) with a reimbursement obligation if we choose not to defend and Customer incurs reasonable costs. Alternatively, offer a hybrid: Redwood controls with option for Customer to take control if Redwood fails to assume defense within 30 days; reimbursement capped at $500,000 (total).

- Escrow: operationally a no-go for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private we can discuss provider escrow/bonding, but for hosted SaaS we should resist. If NeuroBank insists, propose an insurer/letter of credit alternative or short-term holdback limited to a narrow trigger and dollar amount tied to contract value.

- Liability cap: push back on $1M. Counterproposal: greater of $5M or 2x annual contract value, with a sub-cap for indemnity arising from IP claims to avoid unlimited exposure. If they are fixed on $1M, we might trade down through other concessions (e.g., stronger notice, stricter evidence requirements, and insurer offset).

- Evidence requirements: accept NeuroBank's Evidence_Checklist as a starting point but require that claims include specific, verifiable evidence (e.g., copy of assertion, URLs, sample outputs) prior to any remediation or holdback.

Next steps:
1) Marissa: send a short email back with these counters and offer a 30-min call with procurement/legal.
2) Priyom/Rishi: prepare the commercial tradeoffs (discounts / credits) we would consider for a $1M cap or escrow concession.
3) Legal: I can draft the redline text for the carveout and hybrid defense-control language.

I’ll draft the proposed indemnity compromise and share v2 for internal sign-off before we respond.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-30 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form - Indemnity and notice carveouts

Courtney — thanks for the redline and checklist. We want to be collaborative and keep this moving. Attached is a short note summarizing our proposed compromise (Proposed_Indemnity_Compromise.docx). High level: 

- Notice: we can accept a 45-day notice window instead of your requested 30 days.
- AI outputs: we will accept a narrowly-tailored carveout limited to Customer-provided content that is the proximate cause of the claim. We cannot accept a broad blanket exclusion for "model outputs."
- Defense: Redwood will retain primary defense control; Customer may assume defense if we fail to do so within 30 days. If Customer assumes defense, Redwood will reimburse reasonable costs up to a $500,000 cap.
- Escrow: we cannot agree to a general escrow for hosted customers. We can discuss an insurer-backed alternative (letter of credit or escrow for Dedicated deployments only).
- Cap: our counter is the greater of $5M or 2x annual contract value; if NeuroBank must hold to $1M we will need material commercial concessions (e.g., higher unit pricing/shortened term/accelerated payments).

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday to finalize? If procurement needs written sign-off sooner, Kimberly will provide the clean redline text and we can inline the proposed language into the order form.

Thanks — look forward to resolving quickly.

Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Contracts | Redwood Inference
